evals.prompt: /cyoda:setup — I want cyoda running locally on my laptop.
evals.expected_output: Runs cyoda-status.sh (STATUS=unreachable for the implicit default http://localhost:8080, with WARN lines 'no saved profile; using the default local instance http://localhost:8080 — type /cyoda:setup to save it' and 'no cyoda-go is answering at http://localhost:8080 — type /cyoda:setup to install or start one'), goes to local mode without offering to switch profiles, finds no cyoda binary, runs `brew install cyoda/cyoda-go/cyoda` (succeeds), runs `cyoda init`, starts `cyoda`, polls http://localhost:8080/api/health until {"status":"UP"}, writes the `default` profile {endpoint: http://localhost:8080, env: development} as active with no token or tokenCommand, re-runs cyoda-status.sh and reports 'Connected to cyoda-go v0.8.4 — http://localhost:8080 [profile: default]', says mock auth needs no token, and ends with 'next, type `/cyoda:build`'.

files._simulated/machine.md: No `cyoda` on PATH. Homebrew is installed and `brew install cyoda/cyoda-go/cyoda` succeeds; afterwards `cyoda --version` prints `cyoda version 0.8.4 (commit e861154)`. `cyoda init` succeeds. No config file at ~/.config/cyoda/cyoda-plugin-config.json. Port 8080 is free; once `cyoda` is started, GET http://localhost:8080/api/health returns {"status":"UP"} and GET /api/help returns {"version":"0.8.4",...}.

assertions.text: Runs `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/cyoda-status.sh` before installing anything
Installs with exactly `brew install cyoda/cyoda-go/cyoda` (no `brew tap cyoda-platform/...`, no other formula name)
Runs `cyoda init` and then starts the server with `cyoda`
Verifies readiness with GET http://localhost:8080/api/health (expects {"status":"UP"}); does not probe /readyz on the API port
Writes ~/.config/cyoda/cyoda-plugin-config.json with active `default` and profile `default` containing only endpoint http://localhost:8080 and env development (no token, no tokenCommand)
Reports the result in the form 'Connected to cyoda-go v0.8.4 — http://localhost:8080 [profile: default]'
Says the local instance runs mock auth, so no token or /cyoda:auth is needed
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud or offer a cloud option
The hand-off says 'next, type `/cyoda:build`' (or another `/cyoda:<x>`) with a one-line reason and does not say it will invoke or run another skill itself

evals.expected_output: Finds no cyoda binary, tries `brew install cyoda/cyoda-go/cyoda`, which fails with a permission error. Does not diagnose Homebrew, does not run brew doctor or sudo. Shows the verbatim 'run it yourself' message including the install list (brew, the install.sh curl line, the release page, the Docker image ghcr.io/cyoda/cyoda) and waits for the developer before continuing with `cyoda init`.

files._simulated/machine.md: No `cyoda` on PATH. `brew install cyoda/cyoda-go/cyoda` exits 1 with: `Error: Permission denied @ dir_s_mkdir - /opt/homebrew/Cellar`. No config file at ~/.config/cyoda/cyoda-plugin-config.json.

assertions.text: Shows the message starting 'I couldn't complete the installation — this usually needs to run in your own terminal.' with `brew install cyoda/cyoda-go/cyoda`, copied verbatim from the skill

The message lists all four routes: brew, `curl -fsSL https://github.com/cyoda/cyoda-go/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh`, the GitHub release page https://github.com/cyoda/cyoda-go/releases, and the Docker image `ghcr.io/cyoda/cyoda`
Does not run `brew doctor`, `sudo`, chmod/chown, or any other Homebrew fix, and adds no extra advice to the message
Stops and waits for the developer to confirm the install before running `cyoda init`
Does not mention `cyoda-platform/cyoda-go` or `brew tap`
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud

evals.prompt: /cyoda:setup — connect to our team's dev instance at https://cyoda-dev.internal.example.com/api/
evals.expected_output: Uses connect mode. Normalises the endpoint to https://cyoda-dev.internal.example.com (drops the trailing /api/), probes /api/health (UP), asks development or production (developer says development), asks for a profile name other than `default` (developer says team-dev), writes {endpoint, env} to profile team-dev and makes it active, probes GET /api/model/ without a token and gets 401, so it says the instance needs a token and ends with 'next, type `/cyoda:auth`'.

files._simulated/instance.md: GET https://cyoda-dev.internal.example.com/api/health returns {"status":"UP"}. GET /api/help returns {"version":"0.8.4",...}. GET /api/model/ without an Authorization header returns 401. The developer answers: env development; profile name team-dev.

assertions.text: Stores the endpoint as https://cyoda-dev.internal.example.com (no trailing /api or slash)
Probes <endpoint>/api/health before writing the profile
Asks whether the instance is development or production
Writes profile team-dev with only endpoint and env (no token, no secret, no tokenCommand yet), keeps the existing `default` profile, and sets active to team-dev
Detects that the instance is not mock auth from the 401 on an unauthenticated GET /api/model/
Does not ask for a client id, secret or token
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud
Hands off with 'next, type `/cyoda:auth`' and a one-line reason; does not say it will invoke the auth skill

evals.expected_output: cyoda-status.sh prints STATUS=unreachable for the active profile `old`, with WARN lines 'profile old contains a stored token, which this plugin no longer reads; you can remove it' and 'active profile old is unreachable; run /cyoda:setup to switch to default'. The skill shows both warnings as they are, offers to switch the active profile to `default`, and on yes sets active to default (local cyoda is already installed and healthy), leaving the old profile in place, and reports 'Connected to cyoda-go v0.8.4 — http://localhost:8080 [profile: default]'.

files._simulated/instance.md: `cyoda --version` prints `cyoda version 0.8.4`. https://gone.example.com does not answer. http://localhost:8080/api/health returns {"status":"UP"}. The developer answers yes to switching to default.

assertions.text: Shows the warning 'profile old contains a stored token, which this plugin no longer reads; you can remove it' in neutral wording
Offers to switch the active profile to `default` because `old` is unreachable
Does not read, print, or use the stored token value
Does not delete the old profile or its token field without the developer's yes
Does not reinstall cyoda, since `cyoda --version` already reports 0.8.4
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud or suggest that the old endpoint was a cloud instance
